sections.h2: What does the Alton housing market look like?
sections.html:
Alton is a Mississippi River city in Madison County, about 18 miles north of St. Louis, with a low-priced housing market. Owners value their homes at a median $103,700 in the Census five-year survey ending 2024, and 59.9% of homes are occupied by their owners, so a good part of the market is rental.

Census staff counted 25,676 residents in 2020 and estimated 25,013 for July 1, 2025, a 2.6% drop from their base. Most of Alton rises steeply from the waterfront onto bluffs, which gives many streets river views and leaves low-lying blocks exposed to river floods. The city was laid out as a river trading town in January 1818 and later grew around grain, glass, steel and box board.

  • Typical monthly gross rent: $1,015
  • Median household income: $54,568
  • Share of residents in poverty: 21.0%
  • Households: 10,714, averaging 2.30 people
  • Mean commute: 22.7 minutes

sections.h2: How do Alton's bluffs, floods and old streets affect a house sale?
sections.html:
They affect inspections, insurance and buyer expectations more than any other local factor. The city's history notes that the lower levels of Alton flood, that high-water marks are painted on the grain silos near the riverfront, and that the flood of 1993 was the worst of the last century. The city's own website advertises an open house on planned flood mitigation, so ask the city about any project near your block.

Much of the older housing is Victorian Queen Anne, with brick commercial buildings downtown and an unusually high number of brick-paved streets left over from the area's brick factories. Buyers near the river will ask about the flood zone, so gather any elevation certificate or flood insurance history before you list.

sections.h2: Which Alton landmarks and districts draw buyers?
sections.html:
The riverfront, the historic core and the bluff-top residential streets each attract a different buyer. The seventh Lincoln-Douglas debate took place in downtown Alton on October 15, 1858, and the Lyman Trumbull House is a national historic monument. The city has a Historic Preservation Commission, an Appearance Review Commission and a Building Board of Appeals that work alongside the planning staff.

  • The Meeting of the Great Rivers National Scenic Byway and the Great River Road follow the riverfront and the bikeway north of town.
  • Lock and Dam 26 is the newest and busiest lock complex on the main channel of the Mississippi, and the National Great Rivers Museum runs tours of it.
  • The city site lists 19 parks, a marina and a fire department ISO rating of 2.
  • Visitors come for antique shopping, the Argosy Casino and bald eagle watching in winter.

The planning department also administers the Riverfront TIF District and the Hunterstown TIF District and coordinates with Madison County on the Riverbend Enterprise Zone. A property inside one of those boundaries may qualify for redevelopment incentives, so ask the Planning and Development office at 618.463.3500 whether your parcel is inside one.

sections.h2: Which schools and transit options serve Alton?
sections.html:
Alton Community Unit School District 11 serves the bulk of the city, while a small eastern section sits in Bethalto Consolidated Unit School District 8. Alton High School and Alton Middle School are the public secondary schools, and Alton Middle School enrolls roughly 1,500 students and is billed as the largest middle school in the state. Marquette Catholic High School is the private option, and the former Shurtleff College campus is now home to the Southern Illinois University School of Dental Medicine.

Alton station carries Amtrak's Lincoln Service north to Chicago Union Station and south to St. Louis. Madison County Transit buses run in the city with hubs downtown and at the Amtrak station.

sections.h2: What does Alton Code Enforcement require when a house changes occupants?
sections.html:
Alton's Code Enforcement Department performs universal residential occupancy inspections, so a change of occupant can trigger a visit even when ownership stays the same. The department also issues building, demolition, electrical, plumbing, signage, occupancy and agent authorization permits and reviews plans for renovations.

  • Since February 1, 2015, the city has refused to schedule an occupancy inspection until the form names every person moving into the dwelling.
  • For adults the form needs a full name, date of birth and driver's license or state ID number. For children it needs a full name and date of birth.
  • The department cites weeds, junk, trash, derelict vehicles and exterior or interior property maintenance violations, and it sends unresolved citations to court.
  • The city also inspects fire-damaged structures and handles demolition proceedings.

Before you list, call the Code Enforcement Office at 618.463.3500 and ask whether the property has open citations or an unclosed permit. A buyer of the house in any condition inherits those issues, so settling them first keeps the closing date steady.

sections.h2: How does Madison County bill property tax on an Alton house?
sections.html:
Madison County collects in four installments. Bills for the 2025 tax year went out the week of June 9, 2026, and mobile home tax came due August 31.

2026 installment dates published by the Madison County Treasurer
InstallmentDue date in 2026
FirstJuly 9
SecondSeptember 9
ThirdOctober 9
FourthDecember 9

Source: Madison County Treasurer, Frequently Asked Questions.

  • A 1.5% penalty attaches to a late installment every 30 days, and taxes still unpaid go into the annual tax sale.
  • After a tax sale an owner can redeem for two to three years through the County Clerk, paying the entire amount owed.
  • About 220 taxing districts levy against Madison County property, and the assessed value is one third of fair market value.
  • The FAQ lists a $6,000 general homestead exemption, a $5,000 senior homestead exemption, $5,000 returning veterans and $2,000 disabled persons exemptions.
  • The treasurer's FAQ says Madison County does not apply the Property Tax Extension Limitation Law that caps increases in other counties.

Call the Treasurer's Office at (618) 692-6260 for a duplicate bill. State law makes the tax due even when the bill never arrives.

sections.h2: How can an Alton owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
A written complaint goes to the Madison County Board of Review, and it is due 30 days after the assessments are published. Section 16-55(d) of the Property Tax Code sets that deadline, and the county treasurer's FAQ repeats it. Talk first with the township or county assessor, since the Chief County Assessment Office at (618) 692-6270 can explain how the value was set.

You will need evidence that the property is overassessed, such as recent sales of similar Alton houses, an appraisal or documented condition problems. The Board of Review can be reached at (618) 692-6210. An appeal changes the assessed value only, because the tax rate comes from the local taxing districts.

sections.h2: What does the Madison County Recorder need to record an Alton deed?
sections.html:
The Recorder will not accept a deed without an Illinois Department of Revenue transfer declaration (PTAX) or a statement of exemption. The state collects 50 cents on each $500 of taxable consideration under Section 31-10 of the Property Tax Code, and Madison County adds 25 cents on each $500.

  • Each deed carries the grantee's name and address for tax billing, with a Plat Act affidavit attached.
  • A permanent parcel number is required on documents that affect a transfer, by county board resolution.
  • The preparer's name and address must appear on the instrument itself.
  • When paying by check, the recording fee and the transfer tax are paid separately.

The recorder's list of documents includes executor's, administrator's, guardian's and trustee's deeds, so a house sold through an estate is recorded with the same declaration and parcel number requirements.

sections.h2: Which selling routes fit an Alton house?
sections.html: Alton owners can hire an agent, go it alone, or sell outright to a buyer who takes whatever shape the house is in. A listing works best on a clean, move-in ready house in a good school boundary. A private sale suits an owner who already has a buyer lined up. The third route suits a vacant, inherited or damaged house, because the buyer accepts what is there and the closing date can be set around the occupancy inspection and the flood or code questions described above.

faqs.q: How many property tax installments does Madison County have?
faqs.a: Four. For 2025 taxes payable in 2026 they were due July 9, September 9, October 9 and December 9, with mobile home tax due August 31. The Treasurer's Office can give you the schedule on the next bill.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for a late Madison County installment?
faqs.a: A 1.5% penalty is added the day after the deadline and again every 30 days. Delinquency notices go out about a month before the tax sale, and unpaid taxes are sold to a tax buyer.

faqs.q: Does Alton require an occupancy inspection when I sell?
faqs.a: Alton conducts universal residential occupancy inspections, and its policy requires information on every person who will live in the dwelling. Ask Code Enforcement at 618.463.3500 whether your sale or the next tenant triggers one.

faqs.q: How much is the Illinois transfer tax on an Alton sale?
faqs.a: The state rate is 50 cents on each $500 of declared value, and Madison County adds 25 cents on each $500. The Recorder collects both at recording.

faqs.q: When must an Alton assessment complaint be filed?
faqs.a: The filing period is 30 days from publication of the assessments, and the complaint goes to the Madison County Board of Review. Call (618) 692-6210 to confirm how the board takes filings.
